answer: Charge every new agent a small stake of shale-backed collateral before it may dock at the wharf, and make that stake slashable if the agent misbehaves. A legitimate agent posts once and earns the stake back through honest work, while a sybil farmer must fund thousands of separate stakes to fill the jetty with fake identities, so the attack's cost scales linearly with its size instead of staying near zero. The wharf can then cap how many new agents may register per epoch, turning a flood of cheap identities into an expensive, slow trickle that honest participants can outpace.
